items.title: Use confluence analysis in TradingView webhook enrichment
items.body:
## Problem

`POST /api/webhook/alert?useTradingViewData=true` currently enriches TradingView-style alert text through the synchronous MCP enrichment path, but that path only calls `coin_analysis` plus optional `volume_confirmation_analysis`. It does not use the already-integrated `combined_analysis` or `multi_timeframe_analysis` tools before producing the chat alert.

That means a real-time TradingView webhook can be marked bullish/bearish from a single-timeframe technical snapshot even when broader confluence, Reddit/news context, or multi-timeframe alignment would downgrade the setup.

## Trading Hypothesis

Adding optional confluence-aware enrichment for TradingView webhook alerts should reduce noisy real-time alerts and make delivered messages better suited for trade triage. This is signal-quality decision support, not a guarantee of profitable trades.

## Proposed Change

Extend the TradingView MCP alert enrichment path with an opt-in confluence mode:

- add a feature flag or request option for confluence-aware enrichment on `/api/webhook/alert?useTradingViewData=true`
- reuse `combined_analysis` when enabled to include technical, sentiment, news, and confluence fields in the enriched alert
- optionally call `multi_timeframe_analysis` within the existing `TRADINGVIEW_MCP_ENRICHMENT_BUDGET_MS` envelope
- downgrade, annotate, or suppress high-confidence wording when confluence is mixed, bearish against a buy signal, bullish against a sell signal, or unavailable
- preserve the current `coin_analysis` path as the default/fallback until validated
- include machine-readable confluence metadata in dry-run responses so behavior can be tested without sending notifications

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Default webhook behavior remains backward compatible unless the new mode/flag is enabled.
- [ ] Confluence mode calls `combined_analysis` and, if configured, `multi_timeframe_analysis` within the existing enrichment budget.
- [ ] Failures in combined or multi-timeframe calls fail open to the existing `coin_analysis` enrichment path.
- [ ] Enriched alert output includes concise confluence/multi-timeframe reasoning when available.
- [ ] Dry-run responses expose enough structured metadata to verify downgrade/suppression decisions.
- [ ] Unit tests cover aligned, mixed, contradictory, timeout, and unavailable confluence cases.
- [ ] Integration tests cover `/api/webhook/alert?useTradingViewData=true&dryRun=true` and preserve API-key auth, notification routing, MarkdownV2 formatting, and fail-open delivery.
- [ ] If request/response contracts change, `src/openapi/openapi.json` and `CabrosBot.postman_collection.json` are updated.

## Validation Plan

- Start with deterministic MCP fixtures for `coin_analysis`, `combined_analysis`, and `multi_timeframe_analysis`.
- Validate through dry-run webhook calls before enabling notification-delivery changes.
- Compare delivered/dry-run confluence decisions against the shadow-mode metrics proposed in #129 once measurements exist.

## Evidence

- `src/controllers/webhooks/handlers/alert/alert.js:119-139` enables TradingView enrichment only through the webhook query flag and delegates to `processEnrichment()`.
- `src/controllers/webhooks/handlers/alert/grounding.js:163-174` calls `tradingViewMcpService.enrichFromAlertText(text)` when MCP enrichment is enabled.
- `src/services/tradingview/TradingViewMcpService.js:87-91` calls `callCoinAnalysis()` for the webhook enrichment path.
- `src/services/tradingview/TradingViewMcpService.js:104-129` optionally adds only volume confirmation after `coin_analysis`.
- `src/services/tradingview/TradingViewMcpService.js:154-217` already has `combined_analysis` and `multi_timeframe_analysis` wrappers, but they are used by report-style analysis rather than webhook alert enrichment.
- `src/services/tradingview/expandedAnalysisAlertReport.js:41-42` exposes `includeMultiTimeframe` and `analysisMode`, proving the richer MCP data is already part of the repo's TradingView architecture.
- `tests/integration/alert-tradingview-mcp.test.js:55-81` verifies the alert webhook calls `enrichFromAlertText()` but does not cover combined or multi-timeframe confluence.
- Related issues/PRs: #128 covers risk/reward targets for expanded reports; #129 covers shadow-mode outcome tracking; PR #48 and PR #68 added multi-timeframe/combined support to the expanded-analysis endpoint only. No open issue or PR matched this webhook enrichment gap after live dedupe.

## Risks

- Extra MCP calls can increase latency and timeout risk. Keep the mode opt-in, bounded by the existing enrichment budget, and fail open to the current path.
- Confluence wording can create false precision. Phrase it as decision support and keep raw metadata visible in dry-run output.

---

items.title: Add shadow-mode outcome tracking for trading signals
items.body:
## Problem

The repo has alert storage, alert export, scanner jobs, news monitor results, and TradingView MCP reports, but there is no trading-outcome feedback loop. Repo search found no hit-rate, drawdown, PnL, paper-trading, backtest, or future-return tracking for generated signals.

No measurements found.

Without outcome tracking, scanner ranking, news thresholds, prompt tuning, and risk/reward rules cannot be validated against later price movement or false-positive rate.

## Trading Hypothesis

A shadow-mode measurement loop should make future trading-improvement work safer and more testable by comparing generated signals against later market outcomes before changing live delivery behavior. This is a validation/telemetry capability, not a promise of profitability.

## Proposed Change

Add optional shadow-mode outcome tracking for alert-producing trading surfaces:

- record normalized signal metadata for scanner hits, expanded-analysis rows, news alerts, and TradingView-enriched webhook alerts
- capture decision-time fields such as symbol, exchange, timeframe, setup type, score/confidence, side/bias, price, stop, target, sources, and requestId
- evaluate later outcome windows such as `+1h`, `+4h`, `+1D`, and `+1W` using configured market-data providers when available
- expose aggregated metrics through a protected read endpoint or existing alerts summary/export path: hit rate, average return, max adverse excursion, max favorable excursion, drawdown proxy, false-positive candidates, and latency/cost metadata
- keep the feature disabled by default and safe for production shadow-mode rollout

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Shadow-mode storage is controlled by an explicit feature flag and never blocks notification delivery.
- [ ] Generated signals include enough normalized metadata to evaluate future outcomes without parsing chat text.
- [ ] Outcome evaluation handles missing market data as unavailable, not as zero return.
- [ ] Summary/export output reports `No measurements found` when no evaluated records exist.
- [ ] Unit tests cover metadata normalization and outcome math.
- [ ] Integration tests cover protected summary/export behavior, disabled mode, and provider failures.
- [ ] Existing auth, feature gates, idempotency, notification routing, and fail-open alert delivery are preserved.

## Validation Plan

- Start with deterministic fixtures and local provider mocks for outcome windows.
- Add a dry-run/shadow-mode path before using production delivery signals.
- Run focused storage/export tests and one endpoint-level integration test.
- Only use collected metrics to tune thresholds in follow-up issues after enough data exists.

## Evidence

- `src/routes/index.js` mounts protected alert read/export/summary and scanner/job endpoints, but no outcome or backtest endpoint exists.
- `src/controllers/webhooks/handlers/marketScanner/marketScanner.js:118-129` returns scanner delivery summaries, not future price outcomes.
- `src/controllers/webhooks/handlers/newsMonitor/analyzer.js:392-403` caches alert/delivery metadata, not later market outcomes.
- `src/services/tradingview/expandedAnalysisAlertReport.js:196-233` builds rich per-symbol report rows, but no persisted normalized outcome model is produced.
- Repo search found no implementation references for hit rate, drawdown, PnL, paper trading, backtest, future return, or risk outcome metrics beyond generic job delivery outcomes.
- Related issues/PRs: no open PRs and no open/closed issue matches found for trading outcome telemetry or shadow-mode validation.

## Risks

- Outcome tracking can add storage cost and market-data calls. Keep it opt-in, bounded by retention/window limits, and fail-open on provider errors.
- Metrics can be misread as financial advice. Label outputs as historical/shadow-mode diagnostics only.

---

The expanded analysis report already extracts price, RSI, SMA20, MACD, ATR, volume, confluence, news, sentiment, and optional multi-timeframe alignment. But the final trading decision support only includes a suggested stop loss and a broad text suggestion. It does not include take-profit targets, invalidation distance, or risk/reward ratio.

That makes reports less actionable: a setup can look bullish but still have poor upside/downside from the current price.

Adding deterministic risk/reward fields based on available ATR, Bollinger bands, support/resistance, and confluence data should help operators prioritize cleaner setups and avoid low-quality entries. This is decision support, not financial advice or guaranteed profit.

Extend expanded-analysis report generation with risk/reward metadata:

- compute stop/invalidation using the existing ATR/Bollinger fallback path
- compute one or more take-profit targets from nearest resistance, Bollinger upper band, ATR multiples, or available MCP support/resistance fields
- compute `riskRewardRatio` when price, stop, and target are available
- classify setups as `favorable`, `neutral`, or `poor` based on configurable thresholds
- include concise Spanish report lines for target, risk/reward, and invalidation
- include machine-readable fields in API/dry-run responses if the contract is extended

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Expanded report rows include target and risk/reward when enough source data exists.
- [ ] Rows omit or mark risk/reward as unavailable when required data is missing rather than inventing values.
- [ ] Unit tests cover ATR-based, Bollinger-based, support/resistance-based, and missing-data cases.
- [ ] Integration tests cover the rendered report and compact API response shape if changed.

- Add deterministic fixtures to `expanded-analysis-alert-report` tests with known price/ATR/resistance values.

- `src/services/tradingview/expandedAnalysisAlertReport.js:241-248` renders stop loss and a broad suggestion, but no take-profit target or risk/reward ratio.

items.title: Calibrate news confidence with source quality and freshness
items.body:
## Problem

The news monitor currently asks Gemini for `event_category`, `event_significance`, `sentiment_score`, `headline`, and `description`, then computes confidence with a fixed formula: `0.6 * event_significance + 0.4 * abs(sentiment_score)`. The number of grounded sources is logged, but source freshness, source count, domain quality, uncertainty, and event age are not part of the default confidence gate.

That can let stale or thinly sourced news clear the alert threshold if the model assigns strong sentiment/significance.

## Trading Hypothesis

Adding freshness/source-quality penalties and explicit uncertainty fields should reduce false-positive and stale news alerts, improving trade decision support without claiming guaranteed profit.

## Proposed Change

Extend the news-analysis prompt and parser to return decision-support metadata:

- `source_count`, `source_freshness`, `source_quality`, `event_age`, `time_horizon`, `uncertainty_reason`, and `invalidation_hint`
- a deterministic confidence-calibration function that penalizes stale, single-source, or uncorroborated events
- structured alert metadata explaining why confidence passed or failed
- compatibility with the existing optional LLM enrichment path, keeping conservative lower-confidence selection where applicable

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Prompt fallback and Langfuse prompt registry contract include the new metadata fields.
- [ ] Parser clamps/validates new fields and fails open to `event_category: none` on malformed output.
- [ ] Default confidence calculation includes source count/freshness/quality penalties, not only significance and sentiment magnitude.
- [ ] Alerts include a concise confidence reason when delivered.
- [ ] Unit tests cover stale news, single-source news, conflicting/uncertain news, and high-quality multi-source news.
- [ ] Integration tests prove below-threshold events are suppressed while high-quality events still deliver.
- [ ] Existing auth, feature gates, notification routing, and fail-open behavior are preserved.

## Validation Plan

- Add deterministic Gemini fixture responses for fresh vs stale and single-source vs multi-source cases.
- Run focused `gemini`, `analyzer`, and news-monitor integration tests.
- Validate in dry-run/shadow mode before changing production thresholds.

## Evidence

- `src/services/prompts/defaults/news-analysis.user.txt:11-18` defines a narrow JSON schema with only category/significance/sentiment/headline/description.
- `src/services/prompts/defaults/news-analysis.user.txt:36-40` asks for conservative scoring, but does not require source freshness, event age, time horizon, or invalidation data.
- `src/services/grounding/gemini.js:151-169` fetches/searches grounded sources but only folds them into free-form context.
- `src/services/grounding/gemini.js:220-222` computes confidence using only event significance and absolute sentiment.
- `src/controllers/webhooks/handlers/newsMonitor/analyzer.js:340-356` gates delivery directly on that confidence threshold.
- Related issues/PRs: no open PRs and no open/closed issue matches found for news confidence/source-freshness calibration.
